scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Syabru originates among the Himalayan communities of Nepal, serving as a longstanding folk tradition primarily preserved by the Sherpa and Yolmo ethnic groups, alongside other neighboring Himalayan peoples.
The practice has historically accompanied gatherings, festivals, and auspicious events throughout the mountainous regions of Nepal.
on_screen: Map: Nepal · South Asia

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Syabru is performed at gatherings, festivals, and various auspicious events.
It constitutes an essential ritual performance during the celebration of Gyalpo Lhosar.
Community workshops, awareness programmes, and competitions are organized to ensure its ongoing preservation and practice.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is performed to traditional folk songs sung directly by the participants.
Musical accompaniment is frequently provided by traditional instruments, notably the dramnyen lute, which supports the slow communal singing and stepping.
Listen for the Dramnyen.

The sonic texture is defined by collective choral folk singing delivered directly by the dancers as they step. Melodic and rhythmic foundation is provided by the plucked strings of the traditional dramnyen lute, creating a steady, deliberate Himalayan folk soundscape.
